title: Add overlap/added-removed key alignment mode to close the shape -> rvl E_KEY_MISMATCH seam
description:
## Background & Evidence
There is a critical workflow seam between `shape` and `rvl`:
- `shape`'s Row Granularity check is informational ("Always passes"), so `shape nov.csv dec.csv --key loan_id` returns `COMPATIBLE` (exit `0`) when rows are added or removed (even `shape/README.md` line 54 shows `3,214 old / 3,201 new (13 removed, 0 added, 3,201 overlap)` -> `COMPATIBLE`).
- `shape/README.md` then instructs `shape nov.csv dec.csv --key loan_id && rvl nov.csv dec.csv --key loan_id`.
- However, `rvl` enforces exact 1:1 key-set equality and refuses with `E_KEY_MISMATCH` (`action: "escalate"`), and `src/cli/args.rs` currently provides NO flag to compare overlapping keys while reporting added/removed rows.

In real periodic reconciliation workflows (loan payoffs/originations, holdings trades, customer churn), added/removed rows are the normal case.

## Goal
Support deterministic overlap comparison in `rvl` without sacrificing strictness:
- Add `--key-mode exact|overlap` (or `--allow-key-diff`; decide whether `exact` remains default for backward compatibility with `E_KEY_MISMATCH` emitting a literal `next_command` suggesting `--key-mode overlap`!).
- In `overlap` mode:
  1. Report structured `key_membership` summary: `overlap_count`, `old_only_count`, `new_only_count`, bounded sample/list of added & removed keys (respecting `--explicit` redaction rules), and optional column-sum delta attributable to added/removed rows vs. continuing rows.
  2. Run the standard L1 coverage ranking and `REAL_CHANGE`/`NO_REAL_CHANGE` verdict over the aligned overlapping rows (and clarify verdict behavior if continuing rows are unchanged but rows were added/removed!).
- Update `operator.json`, JSON Schema (`rvl.v0` or version bump if breaking), human output, and refusal `next_command` for `E_KEY_MISMATCH`.

## Testing
- Unit + E2E tests covering: exact mode still refuses `E_KEY_MISMATCH` with literal `next_command`; overlap mode with removals-only, additions-only, both, zero overlap (`E_NO_OVERLAP` refusal), and composite keys via `--profile`.
- End-to-end `shape && rvl` pipeline test using the `13 removed, 0 added` scenario.
acceptance_criteria: rvl supports deterministic overlap key alignment with structured added/removed key reporting, E_KEY_MISMATCH emits a runnable next_command, and shape->rvl E2E tests pass with added/removed rows.

Diff scan: no removed assertions, no added #[ignore]. Not verified: optional column-sum delta (not implemented); full suite. Default nightly cannot build polars->ethnum dev-dep (env issue).

title: E_MISSINGNESS and E_MIXED_TYPES should report key value instead of record number in key mode
description: When using --key, refusal messages for E_MISSINGNESS and E_MIXED_TYPES report 'data record 12,775' which is useless — the user chose key mode because row positions don't matter. General principle: any refusal that identifies a specific row should use the key value when --key is specified. Today only E_MISSINGNESS and E_MIXED_TYPES are affected (they fire post-alignment through detect_numeric_columns where KeyAlignedRow.key is available). Fix: extend RowRef with an optional key field, populate it in key mode, thread it into RefusalKind::Missingness and RefusalKind::MixedTypes, and display the key value in both human and JSON output when present. title: rvl ignores composite keys in profile; shape honors them
description:
A frozen profile's 'key:' is a LIST. shape consumes the full composite; rvl silently uses only the first element.

REPRO (public SEC data, CGCMT 2016-P6 ABS-EE):
  profile key: [ORIGINATIONDATE, ORIGINALLOANAMOUNT]
  shape a.csv b.csv --profile p.yaml
    -> 'Key: ORIGINATIONDATE + ORIGINALLOANAMOUNT (unique in both files)' COMPATIBLE, coverage=0.91
  rvl a.csv b.csv --profile p.yaml
    -> 'Alignment: key=ORIGINATIONDATE'  then E_KEY_DUP

IMPACT: this is the documented remediation path when an upstream filer changes its identifier scheme (ASSETNUMBER went from '01A21,02A5,03A2' to '1,2,3' in Jan 2017 for this deal). A natural composite key is the deterministic rekey. shape proves it viable; rvl then refuses on a key the operator did not choose. The two tools disagree about the same profile contract.

EXPECTED: rvl aligns on the full composite key, or refuses explicitly with a typed 'composite keys unsupported' reason rather than silently narrowing to key[0].

The silent narrowing is the real defect - the refusal it emits (E_KEY_DUP) names a key the profile did not declare, which sends the operator to the wrong fix.

Candidate for spine-rules conformance: profile key-list consumption should be a golden rule across all profile-reading operators.
close_reason: Fixed composite profile keys across alignment, analysis, output, refusals, capsules, reproduction minimization, schema, tests, and docs.

title: Add --describe, --schema, and --version flags (parity with suite)
description:
## Problem

rvl is missing three introspection flags that every other spine tool supports:

1. \`--describe\` → \`error: unexpected argument '--describe' found\`
2. \`--schema\` → \`error: unexpected argument '--schema' found\`
3. \`--version\` / \`-V\` → \`error: unexpected argument '--version' found\`

This makes rvl the only tool in the suite that can't be introspected programmatically. An agent trying to auto-discover pipeline capabilities by running \`<tool> --describe\` on each binary hits a wall at rvl.

## Expected

- \`rvl --describe\` → operator.v0 JSON with exit_codes, refusals, pipeline metadata
- \`rvl --schema\` → JSON Schema for rvl output format
- \`rvl --version\` → semver string
- \`rvl -V\` → same

## Notes

- rvl version unknown (can't even query it)
- Discovered during spring11 pipeline introspection
- All other tools (vacuum 0.1.0, hashbytes 0.2.0, fingerprint 0.3.0, shape 0.2.0, lock 0.2.0) support at least --describe and --version
acceptance_criteria: 1. rvl --describe exits 0 and returns valid operator.v0 JSON (schema_version, exit_codes, refusals, pipeline, capabilities). 2. rvl --schema exits 0 and returns JSON Schema for rvl output format. 3. rvl --version and rvl -V print semver string to stdout. 4. All three flags work without positional args. 5. operator.v0 includes pipeline.upstream (shape) and pipeline.downstream (lock).

title: Improve E_MIXED_TYPES error with cross-tab hint
description:
## Problem

When rvl encounters mixed types in a column, the error is correct but gives no guidance:

```
E_MIXED_TYPES: column 'comp_1' contains mixed numeric/non-numeric values
```

In CRE appraisal data, this is almost always because the CSV is a cross-tab (pivot table) where the row label determines value type — e.g., "Occupancy" rows have percentages, "Sales Price" rows have dollars, "Year Built" rows have dates, all in the same comp_1 column.

## Observed behavior (spring11 session)

Ran \`rvl dallas_sales_comp.csv dallas_sales_comp.csv\` as a reproducibility sanity check. Got E_MIXED_TYPES because the sales comp adjustment grid is inherently cross-tab:

| field | comp_1 |
|-------|--------|
| Total Units | 142 |
| Occupancy | 91% |
| Sales Price | \$19,600,000 |
| Year Built | 1983 (2023) |
| Location Adj | 0% |

All values live in comp_1 but have completely different types depending on the field column.

## Suggested improvement

```
E_MIXED_TYPES: column 'comp_1' contains mixed numeric/non-numeric values (5 numeric, 12 non-numeric).
  Hint: If this is a cross-tab where row labels determine value types,
  consider reshaping to long-form or splitting into typed sections
  before comparison.
```

## Notes

- This is a documentation/UX issue, not a logic bug — rvl is correct to refuse
- Cross-tab structures are extremely common in CRE (comp grids, rent rolls, operating statements)

title: Wire witness recording into rvl execution path
description:
## Context

Wire witness into rvl's main execution path. After the pipeline runs and output is formatted, build a witness record and append it to the ledger. Add --no-witness flag.

Depends on: bd-5cm (ledger writer)

## Exact Changes

### 1. Add --no-witness to CLI args

In `src/cli/args.rs`, add:

```rust
/// Disable witness ledger recording
#[arg(long)]
pub no_witness: bool,
```

### 2. Modify `src/lib.rs` — `run()`

After the pipeline produces `result: PipelineResult` (defined in orchestrator.rs:58 as `{ outcome: Outcome, output: String }`) and the output is written to stdout/stderr, add witness recording:

```rust
if !args.no_witness {
    witness::record_run(&args, &result);
}
```

### 3. File bytes for hashing

The orchestrator loads file bytes via `fs::read()` in `parse_csv()` (orchestrator.rs:688), but those bytes are consumed into `ParsedCsv` records and not returned to the caller.

**For v0: re-read files in the witness path.** `record_run()` calls `fs::read()` on each input file, then passes the byte slices to `WitnessRecord::from_run()`, which hashes them via `hash_bytes()`. This doubles I/O but keeps the orchestrator interface unchanged. CSV files are typically small, so this is acceptable.

Note: `hash_file()` (streaming) from bd-met is used only by `hash_self()`. Input file hashing goes through `from_run()` → `hash_bytes()` on pre-loaded bytes.

### 4. Create `witness::record_run()` convenience function

In `src/witness/mod.rs`, add a top-level function that orchestrates the full witness flow:

```rust
pub fn record_run(args: &Args, result: &PipelineResult) {
    // 1. Read both input files via fs::read() (re-read for v0)
    // 2. Read prev from ledger via LedgerWriter::read_prev()
    // 3. Build WitnessRecord via from_run(args, result, old_bytes, new_bytes, ...)
    //    (from_run handles all hashing internally: input bytes, output string, binary)
    // 4. Compute id via record.compute_id()
    // 5. Append to ledger via LedgerWriter::append()
    // All errors logged to stderr, never propagated
}
```

The key types are:
- `Args` — from `cli::args::Args` (the clap-parsed CLI arguments)
- `PipelineResult` — from `orchestrator::PipelineResult` (`{ outcome: Outcome, output: String }`)
- `Outcome` — from `cli::exit::Outcome` (enum: `NoRealChange`, `RealChange`, `Refusal`)

Params extraction lives in `from_run()` (bd-2mb), not here.

## Files to Change

1. `src/cli/args.rs` — add --no-witness flag
2. `src/lib.rs` — add witness call after output
3. `src/witness/mod.rs` — add `record_run()` convenience function

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `rvl old.csv new.csv` creates a witness record at the expected ledger path (use `EPISTEMIC_WITNESS` env var in tests)
- Running `rvl old.csv new.csv --no-witness` creates NO ledger file
- Running rvl twice produces two records with correct `prev` chaining (second record's prev = first record's id)
- Record fields match the actual invocation: `tool="rvl"`, correct file hashes, correct outcome, correct exit_code
- Witness failure does NOT affect exit code — making the ledger path unwritable still lets rvl succeed with the correct exit code
- `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass
notes: Implemented: --no-witness CLI flag, record_run() convenience function in witness/mod.rs, wired into lib.rs::run() after output. 11 unit tests + 9 integration tests passing. All 200 tests pass, clippy clean, fmt clean.

title: Define witness record struct and canonical serialization
description:
## Context

The witness record is a ~300-byte JSONL struct appended after every rvl invocation. It captures what was run, on what inputs, with what params, producing what outcome — all content-addressed.

Depends on: bd-met (blake3 hashing primitives)

## Exact Changes

### 1. Create `src/witness/record.rs`

Define the witness record struct:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct WitnessRecord {
    pub id: String,           // blake3 of canonical self (with id="")
    pub tool: String,         // "rvl"
    pub version: String,      // from env\!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
    pub binary_hash: String,  // blake3 of running binary
    pub inputs: Vec<WitnessInput>,
    pub params: serde_json::Value,
    pub outcome: String,      // "REAL_CHANGE" | "NO_REAL_CHANGE" | "REFUSAL"
    pub exit_code: u8,
    pub output_hash: String,  // blake3 of the output string
    pub prev: Option<String>, // blake3 id of previous ledger record
    pub ts: String,           // ISO 8601 UTC
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct WitnessInput {
    pub path: String,
    pub hash: String,    // "blake3:<hex>"
    pub bytes: u64,
}
```

**Why `tool: String` not `&'static str`:** The struct derives `Deserialize`. Serde cannot borrow a `&'static str` from non-static input (e.g., a `String` read from the ledger file). Using `String` works for both serialization (`"rvl".to_string()`) and deserialization. `read_prev()` (bd-5cm) and the query subcommand (bd-ogo) both deserialize from file-sourced strings.

Note: `Deserialize` is derived because the ledger reader (bd-5cm read_prev) and query subcommand (bd-ogo) both need to parse records back from JSON.

### 2. Canonical JSON helper

Create a shared helper used by BOTH `compute_id()` and the ledger writer (bd-5cm `append()`):

```rust
/// Serialize a WitnessRecord to canonical JSON (sorted keys, single line).
/// serde_json does NOT sort keys when serializing structs directly — it
/// preserves declaration order. We roundtrip through serde_json::Value
/// (whose Map uses BTreeMap by default, which sorts keys) to guarantee
/// sorted output.
pub fn canonical_json(record: &WitnessRecord) -> String {
    let value = serde_json::to_value(record).expect("WitnessRecord is always serializable");
    serde_json::to_string(&value).expect("Value is always serializable")
}
```

This function is the ONLY serialization path for witness records. Both `compute_id()` and `LedgerWriter::append()` (bd-5cm) must use it. This guarantees that `hash(line_in_ledger_with_id_blanked) == record.id`.

**Feature-flag caution:** serde_json's `Map` uses `BTreeMap` by default but switches to `IndexMap` (insertion order) if the `preserve_order` feature is activated anywhere in the dependency graph. The project's dev-dependencies (polars) could activate this. The canonical JSON test (acceptance criterion below) must verify ALPHABETICAL key order explicitly, not just that keys match the serialization round-trip. If this test ever fails in CI, the fix is to walk the `Value` recursively and sort keys into a `BTreeMap` before serializing.

### 3. Implement `WitnessRecord::compute_id()`

```rust
pub fn compute_id(&mut self) {
    self.id = String::new();
    let canonical = canonical_json(self);
    self.id = format\!("blake3:{}", hash_bytes(canonical.as_bytes()));
}
```

### 4. Implement `WitnessRecord::from_run()`

Constructor that takes:
- `args: &Args` (CLI params)
- `result: &PipelineResult` (outcome + output string from orchestrator)
- `old_bytes: &[u8], new_bytes: &[u8]` (file contents for hashing)
- `old_path: &str, new_path: &str`
- `prev: Option<String>` (previous record id)

Builds the full record: input hashes via `hash_bytes()`, output hash via `hash_bytes()`, exit code via `exit_code(result.outcome)`, timestamp via `std::time::SystemTime`.

Params are extracted from Args inside `from_run()`:
```json
{
    "delimiter": null,
    "json": true,
    "key": "loan_id",
    "threshold": 0.95,
    "tolerance": 1e-9
}
```
Only params affecting comparison results. Exclude --no-witness and positional paths. Build via `serde_json::json\!()` macro (produces sorted BTreeMap keys).

## Files to Change

1. `src/witness/record.rs` — new file
2. `src/witness/mod.rs` — add `pub mod record;`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `WitnessRecord::from_run()` produces a record with all fields populated
- `compute_id()` is deterministic — same inputs produce same id
- `compute_id()` changes when any field changes
- `canonical_json()` output has ALPHABETICALLY sorted keys (verified by checking key order against a hardcoded expected ordering: binary_hash, exit_code, id, inputs, outcome, output_hash, params, prev, tool, ts, version)
- `params` captures key, threshold, tolerance, delimiter, json from Args
- `cargo test` passes with all new unit tests

title: Define witness.v0 JSON Schema and validation tests
description:
## Context

The witness record schema needs a canonical JSON Schema definition in the epistemic meta-repo (when it's created) and an embedded schema in rvl for --schema/--describe compatibility. This issue covers the schema definition and validation tests.

Depends on: bd-2mb (witness record struct)

## Exact Changes

### 1. Create `docs/witness.v0.schema.json`

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the witness record:

- `id`: string, pattern `^blake3:[0-9a-f]{64}$`
- `tool`: string, minLength 1
- `version`: string, pattern `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+`
- `binary_hash`: string, pattern `^blake3:[0-9a-f]{64}$`
- `inputs`: array of objects with `path` (string), `hash` (string, blake3 pattern), `bytes` (integer, minimum 0)
- `params`: object (additionalProperties allowed — tool-specific)
- `outcome`: string (enum values are tool-specific, but must be non-empty)
- `exit_code`: integer, minimum 0, maximum 2
- `output_hash`: string, pattern `^blake3:[0-9a-f]{64}$`
- `prev`: string or null (blake3 pattern when present)
- `ts`: string, format date-time (ISO 8601)

Required: all fields.

### 2. Add schema validation test

In `tests/`, add a test that:
1. Builds a WitnessRecord via `from_run()`
2. Serializes to JSON
3. Validates against the schema using `jsonschema` crate (dev-dependency)
4. Asserts validation passes

### 3. Add a golden witness record fixture

Create `tests/fixtures/witness/golden-record.json` with a hand-crafted, known-good witness record. Test that it validates against the schema and that deserializing + re-serializing produces identical output (canonical JSON stability).

## Files to Change

1. `docs/witness.v0.schema.json` — new file
2. `Cargo.toml` — add `jsonschema` to dev-dependencies
3. `tests/witness_schema.rs` — new test file
4. `tests/fixtures/witness/golden-record.json` — new fixture

## Tests

- Schema validation passes for well-formed records
- Schema validation fails for records with missing required fields
- Schema validation fails for malformed blake3 hashes
- Golden record round-trips through serialize/deserialize without mutation

title: Add rvl --exhaustive audit mode
description:
Background
- Future roadmap item after compare retirement.
- RVL's default contract remains a numeric explanation tool: smallest contributor prefix, `MAX_CONTRIBUTORS`, and `E_DIFFUSE` when broad change cannot be explained compactly.
- Audit/debug workflows sometimes need every changed numeric cell after RVL has already done the hard work: parsing, alignment, profile scoping, and registry-backed header resolution.

Goal
- Add `rvl --exhaustive` as an explicit exhaustive numeric audit mode that enumerates every changed numeric cell above tolerance in aligned rows and common/profile-scoped numeric columns.

Dependencies
- Depends on bd-3vp so audit output inherits profile `column_registry` header resolution.

Scope
- Reuse existing alignment, key/profile behavior, `column_registry` header canonicalization, numeric parsing, tolerance, capsule, witness, and refusal semantics.
- Compare only numeric columns selected by current RVL rules.
- Preserve default behavior exactly when `--exhaustive` is not set.
- Bypass `E_DIFFUSE` only in exhaustive mode.

Non-goals
- Not a text/string diff.
- Not a schema diff.
- Not added/removed row enumeration beyond existing key/row-count/key-mismatch refusal semantics.
- Not fuzzy matching or MDM-like comparison.
design:
Implementation outline
1. Add CLI flags: `--exhaustive` and `--max-audit-changes <n>` with a conservative default.
2. Extend JSON output with `mode: explain|exhaustive_numeric` and an `audit` object.
3. Refactor diff accumulation so exhaustive mode can collect all changed numeric contributors while default mode still uses the top-25 heap.
4. Preserve deterministic contributor ordering: contribution desc, row_id asc, column asc.
5. In exhaustive mode, skip `evaluate_coverage`/`E_DIFFUSE`; output REAL_CHANGE if any changed numeric cells exist, otherwise NO_REAL_CHANGE.
6. Add `E_AUDIT_LIMIT` refusal if changed-cell count exceeds `--max-audit-changes`.
7. Update human output to render audit wording while preserving redaction-by-default and `--explicit`.
8. Update capsule/witness/operator/schema docs so audit mode is reproducible and discoverable.

Resolved open questions
- `contributors` contains all emitted changed numeric cells in exhaustive mode.
- `metrics.total_change` and shares keep numeric meanings; coverage is 1.0 when all changed numeric cells are emitted.
- `E_MISSINGNESS`, `E_MIXED_TYPES`, `E_NO_NUMERIC`, `E_NEED_KEY`, and parse/key refusals still apply.
- String/field changes are separate follow-up work, not part of this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Default RVL output and JSON fixtures remain unchanged unless `--exhaustive` is set.
2. `--exhaustive` emits every changed numeric cell above tolerance for row-order mode and key mode.
3. Broad changes that currently produce `E_DIFFUSE` produce REAL_CHANGE in `--exhaustive` mode when under the audit limit.
4. `--max-audit-changes` refuses with `E_AUDIT_LIMIT` when the changed numeric cell count exceeds the configured limit.
5. Exhaustive contributors are sorted deterministically by contribution desc, row_id asc, column asc.
6. Redacted output remains the default; `--explicit` shows numeric old/new/delta values.
7. JSON output includes `mode: "exhaustive_numeric"` and `audit.numeric_changes_emitted`.
8. Human output uses audit wording and does not claim a smallest explanation set.
9. Capsule replay works for exhaustive runs.
10. Witness params capture `exhaustive` and `max_audit_changes`.
11. Tests cover no-change, single change, diffuse broad change, key mode, row-order mode, audit limit refusal, redaction, explicit output, JSON shape, deterministic ordering, and capsule replay.
12. Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test`.

Spec source: docs/PLAN_RVL.md > Audit Extensions > Exhaustive numeric audit (`--exhaustive`).
Blocked by bd-3vp. After this lands, implement exact field-change audit in the dependent follow-up bead.

title: Honor profile column_registry when resolving dataset headers
description:
Background
- profile v0.3.0 added optional `column_registry` support so profiles can name canonical column IDs while datasets use heterogeneous raw headers.
- RVL currently ignores `column_registry`; it parses only `profile_id`, `profile_sha256`, `include_columns`, and `key`, then applies profile scoping to locally normalized raw headers.
- This prevents RVL from comparing semantically identical datasets whose headers differ by vendor/source/vintage spelling.

Goal
- Honor an active profile's `column_registry` during dataset header resolution so RVL can compare canonical profile columns against raw aliased CSV headers deterministically.

Scope
- Active only when `--profile` or `--profile-id` resolves a profile containing `column_registry`.
- Resolve relative registry paths relative to the resolved profile file.
- Use canon-style registry directory mappings where entries with `canonical_type == "column_name"` map exact raw header aliases to canonical column IDs.
- Canonicalize headers before key lookup, profile include scoping, column intersection, numeric typing, counts, contributors, capsule, and witness metadata.
- Preserve default behavior exactly when no profile registry is active.

Non-goals
- No fuzzy matching or case/punctuation normalization.
- No remote registry fetching.
- No value canonicalization.
- No composite key support.
- No arbitrary non-UTF-8 alias strings in registry JSON.
design:
Implementation outline
1. Extend `src/profile.rs` profile parsing to retain `column_registry` and the resolved profile source path.
2. Add registry loading in `src/profile.rs`: read `registry.json`, then filename-sorted JSON mapping files except `registry.json` and `_build.json`; use only `canonical_type == "column_name"`; first mapping wins.
3. Add a deterministic registry content hash over the registry files used for resolution.
4. Extend `ActiveProfile`/`ProfileRunInfo` in `src/orchestrator.rs` with optional header alias map, registry ref/path/hash, and source profile path.
5. Change `parse_csv` to accept optional header aliases and apply them after existing RVL header normalization but before duplicate detection. Duplicate canonicalized headers refuse with existing `E_HEADERS`.
6. Add `E_PROFILE_REGISTRY` refusal for missing/unreadable/malformed registry references and render it in human/JSON/operator output.
7. Update capsule handling to copy the active registry into the capsule and rewrite local `profile.yaml` so replay is independent of original profile/registry paths.
8. Update witness params to record registry activation and deterministic registry hash when a registry is active.
9. Update README/operator/schema docs to document profile column registry behavior.

Resolved open questions
- Profile `key` and `include_columns` are interpreted against canonicalized header names.
- Output contributor labels use canonical header IDs.
- Two raw headers mapping to one canonical ID are a refusal, not a merge.
- Existing exact-match RVL semantics remain unchanged except for explicit registry alias replacement under an active profile.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With no active profile registry, all existing profile and non-profile behavior remains byte-for-byte compatible except for intentional doc/operator additions.
2. A profile with `column_registry`, canonical `key`, and canonical `include_columns` successfully compares CSVs whose raw headers are registry aliases.
3. Key lookup works when the profile key is canonical, e.g. `loan_id_number`, and the dataset header is raw, e.g. `Loan Number`.
4. Column counts, numeric column counts, contributors, JSON identifiers, and human labels use resolved canonical header IDs.
5. Relative `column_registry` paths resolve relative to the profile YAML file for both `--profile <path>` and `--profile-id <id>`.
6. Missing, unreadable, or malformed registry files produce structured REFUSAL `E_PROFILE_REGISTRY` with actionable detail and Next guidance.
7. Two headers that canonicalize to the same name produce REFUSAL `E_HEADERS`.
8. Registry entries whose `canonical_type` is not `column_name` are ignored.
9. `--capsule-out` with registry-backed profile writes replayable artifacts; `replay.sh` succeeds without original profile/registry paths.
10. Witness params include registry activation metadata and deterministic registry content hash when active.
11. Tests cover direct `--profile`, path-like `--profile-id`, HOME-resolved `--profile-id`, duplicate canonical headers, missing registry refusal, malformed mapping refusal, ignored non-column mappings, and capsule replay.
12. Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test`.
notes:
Spec source: docs/PLAN_RVL.md > Epistemic Spine Extensions > Column registry-backed header canonicalization.
External source: profile:bd-2t5 / github:cmdrvl/profile#3.
Suggested fixtures can be copied/adapted from `/Users/zac/Source/cmdrvl/profile/tests/fixtures/registries/annex_columns_v0` and `loan_tape_alt_headers.csv`.
This bead should be completed before `bd-3on` exhaustive audit mode so exhaustive output inherits resolved profile header semantics.

title: Allow blank-to-numeric nullity flips in --non-numeric mode instead of aborting with E_MISSINGNESS
description:
Reproduced on rvl 0.8.0: `rvl old.csv new.csv --key id --non-numeric --json` aborts with exit 2 `E_MISSINGNESS` (`numeric-vs-missing mismatch`) whenever an otherwise numeric column has a cell that transitions between blank/missing in old and a number (e.g. `7`) in new.

In src/orchestrator.rs (~lines 933-945 and 1660-1685), column typing runs strict numeric missingness refusal before `--non-numeric` can classify nullity flips. However, `--non-numeric` explicitly documents nullity-flip comparison (`Use --non-numeric for deterministic date, categorical, text, nullity and row-churn comparison`), and blank-to-numeric transitions are ubiquitous in real spreadsheets.

Fix: in `--non-numeric` mode, record blank<->numeric transitions under `non_numeric.nullity_flips` (and `field_changes`, redacted by default) instead of refusing with `E_MISSINGNESS`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rvl old new --key id --non-numeric --json` succeeds (exit 1 REAL_CHANGE) on a table with a blank->numeric or numeric->blank transition, recording it in `non_numeric.nullity_flips`.
- Default numeric mode (without `--non-numeric`) preserves existing `E_MISSINGNESS` contract.
- Default redaction holds (no raw values leaked without `--explicit`).
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator on an exact git-archive export of origin/main 3d2b051 (code commits 4b2d99f bd-ez4 and 1b69304 bd-3xw; 3d2b051 is bead text), the repo's own target under the shared cargo lock: cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast, totalled from the raw log: 504 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. GitHub CI on 3d2b051 and 1b69304: success. Diff scan of b48ea2a..3d2b051 on src and tests: 0 assertions removed, 0 #[ignore], 0 #[allow] added, Cargo.toml untouched. Hostile checks on the built binary vs the RELEASED rvl 0.8.0 Intel macOS binary, my own fixture (old.csv: key KEYCANARY1 with a blank CANARYCOL cell, KEYCANARY2 = 5; new.csv: KEYCANARY1 = 77, KEYCANARY2 = 6). SPECIFIC (bd-3xw, nullity flips): 'rvl old new --key id --non-numeric --json' on the blank-to-77 pair: RELEASED 0.8.0 exits 2 E_MISSINGNESS (the bug); NEW exits 1 REAL_CHANGE with non_numeric.nullity_flips = [{column: [REDACTED], became_null: 0, became_non_null: 1}] and 0 canary hits (key, column and value redacted by default); with --explicit the names appear. Default numeric mode (no --non-numeric) still refuses E_MISSINGNESS, so the numeric contract is unchanged (also an explicit pane test). The pane's planted negative (strict typing forced back on makes 5 of 6 new tests fail) is in its evidence; I did not re-run it. NOT verified: numeric_to_blank on its own in my run (the pane's test covers both directions), --non-numeric with row-order mode, large files.

title: Add rvl --audit-fields exact field-change audit
description:
Background
- `--exhaustive` numeric audit intentionally does not detect string/text field changes.
- Some audit workflows need to know that profile-scoped descriptive fields changed, but those changes must not be folded into numeric contribution math.

Goal
- Add explicit exact field-change audit for profile-scoped non-numeric columns as an opt-in extension to exhaustive mode.

Scope
- Valid only with `--exhaustive`.
- Requires active `--profile` or `--profile-id`.
- Reuses RVL alignment, profile scoping, and `column_registry` header canonicalization.
- Compares common/profile-scoped non-numeric columns by exact parsed CSV field bytes.
- Emits field changes separately from numeric contributors.

Non-goals
- No fuzzy matching.
- No case folding, trimming, punctuation normalization, or semantic text equivalence.
- No field-change contribution scores or coverage percentages.
- No row-typed/cross-tab inference.
design:
Implementation outline
1. Add `--audit-fields` CLI flag, valid only with `--exhaustive`.
2. Refuse `--audit-fields` without an active profile using `E_AUDIT_FIELDS_REQUIRES_PROFILE`.
3. Extend column classification so exhaustive mode can identify profile-scoped common columns that are not numeric and are safe for exact field comparison.
4. Preserve existing `E_MIXED_TYPES` behavior for mixed numeric/non-numeric columns; this bead does not implement row-typed inference.
5. Compare field values by exact parsed CSV bytes after record-width normalization. Do not trim, normalize, or interpret missing tokens.
6. Add `field_changes[]` to JSON, separate from numeric `contributors`.
7. Field changes are redacted by default. Include `old` and `new` string values only with `--explicit`.
8. Human output prints a bounded field-change section after numeric audit output.
9. `--max-audit-changes` applies to combined numeric + field changes; exceedance uses `E_AUDIT_LIMIT`.
10. Update capsule, witness, operator/schema, README, and PLAN references.

Resolved open questions
- Field changes affect the top-level outcome: any numeric or field change under audit mode yields REAL_CHANGE.
- Field changes do not affect numeric metrics, total_change, top_k_coverage, shares, or contributor ranking.
- Key columns are never emitted as field changes.
- Profile scoping is required to avoid dumping arbitrary text columns by accident.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `--audit-fields` without `--exhaustive` refuses or fails CLI validation deterministically.
2. `--audit-fields --exhaustive` without an active profile refuses with `E_AUDIT_FIELDS_REQUIRES_PROFILE`.
3. With a profile, exact changes in profile-scoped non-numeric common columns are emitted in `field_changes[]`.
4. A run with no numeric changes but at least one field change returns REAL_CHANGE.
5. A run with no numeric or field changes returns NO_REAL_CHANGE.
6. Field changes are redacted by default and include old/new values only with `--explicit`.
7. Field change ordering is deterministic: row_id asc, column asc.
8. `column_registry` canonical header IDs are used for field-change column names.
9. `--max-audit-changes` counts numeric and field changes together and refuses with `E_AUDIT_LIMIT` if exceeded.
10. Existing `E_MIXED_TYPES` behavior is preserved for mixed numeric/non-numeric columns.
11. Tests cover profile-required refusal, CLI incompatibility, string-only change, mixed numeric+field changes, redaction, explicit values, registry-backed headers, audit limit, deterministic ordering, and capsule replay.
12. Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test`.
notes:
Spec source: docs/PLAN_RVL.md > Audit Extensions > Exact field-change audit (`--audit-fields`).
Depends on bd-3on because this is an extension to exhaustive audit mode, not a standalone string diff feature.

CONTRACT TODAY: docs/PLAN_RVL.md says numeric values must parse as finite f64 (l.144), old/new/delta/contribution/share/cumulative_share are JSON numbers (finite) (l.477), total_change == 0 is the ONLY route to NO REAL CHANGE (l.345), and when a deterministic verdict is impossible rvl refuses loudly (l.51). operator.json and README list refusal codes; none covers overflow. Nothing says what happens when finite inputs give a non-finite result.
EVERY PLACE A FLOAT CAN GO NON-FINITE (inputs finite: parse.rs rejects non-finite; --tolerance/--threshold are rejected if non-finite):
1. diff/tolerance.rs apply: delta = new - old can be +-inf; abs -> inf; max_abs_delta -> inf; contribution -> inf (inf <= any finite tolerance is false). NaN is impossible here (needs inf - inf).
2. diff/heap.rs DiffAccumulator::observe: total_change += contribution -> inf (one inf contribution, or finite ones whose sum passes f64::MAX). Guarded only by debug_assert (panic in debug, silent in release).
3. orchestrator.rs top_k_coverage: sum(top 25) / total_change -> inf/inf = NaN (JSON null). The top-k sum runs in a different order over a subset, so at the f64::MAX edge it could overflow even if total_change did not.
4. diff/coverage.rs evaluate_coverage: !total_change.is_finite() -> NoChange. THIS is the line that turns overflow into NO_REAL_CHANGE. Its cumulative sum can also overflow as in 3.
5. shares (build_json_contributors, build_human_contributors, build_capsule_contributor_summary): contribution/total and the cumulative share; non-finite only if 1-4 already happened.
6. audit path (--exhaustive / --audit-fields / --non-numeric): never calls evaluate_coverage; with total_change = inf it renders REAL_CHANGE with deltas serialized as null (schema violation, not a false NO). Same root.
7. row-order mode: total_change > 0 gates shuffle detection (inf passes). collect_details re-applies tolerance only on the explainable path.
Not overflow: precision above 2^53 (documented in the plan); a tolerance near f64::MAX (finite deltas within it are still zero); date/byte-length arithmetic in non-numeric mode is integer.
CHOICE: a typed refusal, new code E_NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, exit 2, never a verdict. Why not 'correct arithmetic': scaling could rescue the coverage RATIO, but the delta of 1e308 -> -1e308 is not representable at all, so delta/contribution/total_change would have to be null or strings, breaking the finite-JSON-number contract (l.477) and making a verdict whose own evidence cannot be printed; arbitrary precision needs a dependency (excluded). Refusal matches l.51.
SHAPE: detail {quantity: 'delta' | 'total_change', column, key | record, file: none}. column/key follow the bd-ez4 redaction (redacted:ref:c1 / k1, keyed HMAC with RVL_REDACTION_KEY; exact under --explicit). The cell named is the first one, in rvl's deterministic observation order, at which the delta is non-finite or the running total stops being finite. Metrics null and numeric_cells_checked/changed null (they would be infinite/partial). next: express the values in a larger unit (the same factor in both files), or scope columns with a profile, then rerun.
IMPLEMENTATION AT THE ROOT: DiffAccumulator records the first overflow instead of debug_asserting; evaluate_coverage returns a new Overflow decision for a non-finite total or non-finite sum and can no longer return NoChange for them; the orchestrator refuses once, after the row-order E_NEED_KEY gate (a misaligned reorder is the likelier cause there and the plan requires E_NEED_KEY first) and before the audit-limit, audit-mode and coverage branches, so no output path can see a non-finite total. Docs: PLAN_RVL.md, operator.json, README.
TESTS: the four regression tests from the bd-9ss comment (the tie one goes with bd-fyj). They assert 'exit 1 or 2, no panic, not NO_REAL_CHANGE', so a refusal satisfies them unchanged; I add exact-code, redaction, --exhaustive, row-order and tolerance cases, and re-include the overflow domain in the property suite.

title: rvl --non-numeric with a stock frozen profile reports numeric changes as categorical and hides the real categorical transition
description:
Found by the cross-repo E2E harness (cmdrvl/cmdrvl cmd-nal) with the released rvl 0.9.2 and profile 0.12.1 binaries. Synthetic data only.

Repro:
1. old.csv and new.csv with columns loan_id, balance (decimal), status (a few repeated words). Change balance in two rows and status in one row from watchlist to delinquent. Six rows are enough.
2. profile draft init old.csv --out draft.yaml --key loan_id
3. profile freeze draft.yaml --family e2e.loans --version 0 --out frozen.yaml
   (the draft types balance as "number" and every string column, including status, as "text")
4. rvl old.csv new.csv --key loan_id --non-numeric --json --explicit
5. rvl old.csv new.csv --profile frozen.yaml --non-numeric --json --explicit

Observed:
- With --key: categorical_transitions has one entry, status watchlist -> delinquent; text_churn is empty. This matches the data.
- With --profile: categorical_transitions has two entries, both for the numeric column balance, with the raw old and new numbers as category values; the real status change is demoted to text_churn (changed_rows 1) with no transition.
CSV and Parquet gave the same result in this comparison, and XLSX gives the same counts in the suite. numeric_cells_changed stays correct in numeric mode.

Cause, from reading v0.9.2 src/orchestrator.rs:
- the non-numeric column selection keeps any common column that has a profile type, even a numeric one; "number" is not an override rvl knows, so it falls through to cardinality inference and a small numeric column becomes categorical;
- the override "text" means "never categorical", while profile writes "text" as the plain data type of any string column.
So the two tools use the word differently and a stock profile changes the answer.

Expected: a profile produced by profile draft init and freeze does not move numeric columns into categorical analysis, and does not hide a categorical transition. The fix may belong in rvl (ignore or normalize the types it does not define, and agree what "text" means) or in profile's vocabulary.

The E2E suite lists this as a named known failure tied to this bead and fails when the behaviour changes, so update cmdrvl/cmdrvl e2e/known_failures.json together with the fix.

title: Bakeoff harness should skip sep= and blank records like parser
description: Issue: benches/bakeoff.rs does not mirror parser pre-header handling. When RVL_BAKEOFF_DELIMITER is set, choose_dialect returns skip_sep=false, so a leading sep= directive is counted as a data row. title: Add blake3 dependency and witness hashing primitives
description:
## Context

Witness records require BLAKE3 hashes of input files, the tool binary, and the structured output. rvl currently has no hashing dependency.

## Exact Changes

### 1. Add blake3 to Cargo.toml

```toml
[dependencies]
blake3 = "1"
```

### 2. Create `src/witness/mod.rs` and `src/witness/hash.rs`

Implement three functions:

- `hash_bytes(data: &[u8]) -> String` — BLAKE3 of an in-memory byte slice. Returns hex-encoded hash (no prefix — callers add `blake3:` when building records). This is the primary hashing path: used by `from_run()` (bd-2mb) to hash input file bytes and output strings, and by `compute_id()` to hash canonical JSON.
- `hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — streaming BLAKE3 of file contents using `blake3::Hasher` with 16KB buffer reads. Returns hex-encoded hash. Used only by `hash_self()` to hash the running binary without loading it fully into memory.
- `hash_self() -> Result<String>` — BLAKE3 of the running binary via `std::env::current_exe()` → `hash_file()`. Compute once and cache in a `std::sync::OnceLock<String>`.

### 3. Add `pub mod witness;` to `src/lib.rs`

## Files to Change

1. `Cargo.toml` — add blake3 dependency
2. `src/witness/mod.rs` — new module (create)
3. `src/witness/hash.rs` — hashing functions (create)
4. `src/lib.rs` — add `pub mod witness;`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `blake3` appears in Cargo.toml dependencies
- `hash_bytes(b"hello")` returns expected BLAKE3 hex string
- `hash_file()` on a temp file matches `hash_bytes()` of the same content
- `hash_self()` returns a non-empty string and is stable across repeated calls
- `cargo check --all-targets` passes
- `cargo test` passes with all new unit tests

title: Add witness query subcommand for ledger reads
description:
## Context

The witness query CLI provides basic read access to the ledger. For v0, this is a sequential scan of the JSONL file with filtering. It ships as a subcommand of rvl initially (not a separate binary), since rvl is the only witness-producing tool.

Depends on: bd-2im (witness wired into rvl)

## Exact Changes

### 1. Add `witness` subcommand to rvl CLI

Restructure rvl's CLI to support subcommands. The default behavior (no subcommand) remains the comparison pipeline. The `witness` subcommand provides ledger queries.

```
rvl <old.csv> <new.csv> [OPTIONS]          # existing behavior (default)
rvl witness query [FILTERS]                # query the ledger
rvl witness last                           # show the last record
rvl witness count [FILTERS]                # count matching records
```

Use clap's subcommand support. The comparison pipeline is the default when positional args are provided. The witness subcommand activates when `witness` is the first arg.

### 2. Implement query filters

```
--tool <name>           Filter by tool name (always "rvl" for now)
--since <date>          Records after ISO 8601 date
--until <date>          Records before ISO 8601 date
--outcome <outcome>     Filter by outcome (REAL_CHANGE, NO_REAL_CHANGE, REFUSAL)
--input-hash <hash>     Records that analyzed a file with this hash
--limit <n>             Return at most n records (default: 20)
--json                  Output as JSON array (default: human-readable table)
```

### 3. Implement `witness last`

Print the most recent witness record. Useful for scripting:

```bash
rvl witness last --json | jq '.id'
```

### 4. Implement `witness count`

Print the count of matching records. Supports same filters as query.

```bash
rvl witness count --outcome REFUSAL --since 2026-01-01
# 7
```

### 5. Human-readable output format

For `witness query` without --json, print a compact table:

```
ID (short)  Timestamp            Outcome         Inputs
blake3:9f2a 2026-02-23T19:45:12Z REAL_CHANGE     nov.csv → dec.csv
blake3:ab01 2026-02-23T18:30:00Z NO_REAL_CHANGE  old.csv → new.csv
```

### 6. Performance

Sequential scan of JSONL is fine for v0. 100K records ≈ 30MB, scans in <1s. No indexing needed.

## Files to Change

1. `src/cli/args.rs` — restructure for subcommand support (careful: must not break existing positional-arg behavior)
2. `src/witness/query.rs` — new file: query logic
3. `src/witness/mod.rs` — add `pub mod query;`
4. `src/lib.rs` — route to witness subcommand when applicable

## Tests

- Integration test: write 5 records, query with --outcome filter, verify correct subset returned
- Integration test: --since and --until filter by timestamp
- Integration test: --input-hash finds records that touched a specific file
- Integration test: --limit truncates results
- Integration test: witness last returns the most recent record
- Integration test: witness count returns correct integer
- Integration test: empty ledger returns empty results (not an error)
close_reason: Aligned witness query output/empty-result semantics and expanded integration coverage

description:
Today `rvl` focuses strictly on numeric materiality (and refuses with `E_NO_NUMERIC` on string-only tables), missing critical non-numeric changes across aligned datasets (status/flag flips, date extensions/slips, newly populated/wiped fields, and row additions/removals).

Add an opt-in, 100% domain-agnostic non-numeric comparison mode (`--non-numeric` flag and/or `rvl compare` subcommand; default `rvl` numeric behavior and `rvl.v0` golden outputs remain 100% backwards-compatible).

HARD DESIGN RULE: ZERO hardcoded domain/column names. Every common non-numeric column is classified purely from its data distribution (with optional overrides from a frozen `profile` `columns.<col>.type`):
1. `date`: >= 95% of non-null values parse as unambiguous calendar dates (ISO-8601 / Excel / normalized dates) -> emit exact signed day deltas (`+365d`, `-60d`), ranked by `abs(days)`.
2. `categorical`: low cardinality (`distinct <= 50` or `distinct / rows <= 0.05`, configurable) -> emit grouped `(old -> new)` transition counts + affected row keys.
3. `text`: high-cardinality strings/IDs/notes -> emit changed row count + byte-length delta without drowning out discrete transitions or dumping raw prose.
4. Cross-cutting: `nullity_flips` (`null <-> non-null` per column) and `row_churn` (added/removed keys from `bd-16z`).

Zero-retention invariant: under default mode (no `--explicit`), redact literal keys and cell values to structural slots, transition counts, day deltas, and hashed value tokens; expose literal values/keys only when `--explicit` is passed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Zero hardcoded column names or domain heuristics anywhere in source.
- Automatically classifies `date`, `categorical`, and `text` columns from value distributions, honoring optional `profile` column type overrides.
- String-only / date-only tables succeed cleanly under `--non-numeric` (do not hit `E_NO_NUMERIC`).
- Default output (without `--explicit`) passes canary leak tests proving zero raw cell values or keys appear in stdout or witness records.
- Structured JSON output (`date_shifts[]`, `categorical_transitions[]`, `nullity_flips[]`, `text_churn[]`, `row_churn`) is deterministic, sorted, and directly consumable by `assess`.

title: Redact raw contributor row_id, row_key, and column names in default numeric mode when --explicit is not set
description:
Reproduced on rvl 0.9.0 against composite-key Parquet inputs:
In default numeric mode (without `--explicit`), `Contributor::new` (src/output/json.rs:167-203) correctly omits `old`, `new`, `delta`, and `contribution`, but still emits raw `row_id` (e.g. `"u8:D01 + u8:L1002"`), raw `row_key` (`["u8:D01", "u8:L1002"]`), and raw `column` (`"u8:current_balance"`) in stdout JSON and human output.

By contrast, `--non-numeric` mode (and refusal payloads fixed in bd-ez4) redact keys and columns to ordinal refs (`redacted:ref:k1`, `redacted:ref:c1` / `[REDACTED]`) or keyed HMAC under `RVL_REDACTION_KEY`. Whenever a dataset is keyed by PII or client identifiers (borrower name, SSN, email, account holder), default numeric `rvl` leaks raw key values without `--explicit`.

Fix: apply the same ordinal-ref / `RVL_REDACTION_KEY` HMAC redaction to numeric `contributors` (`row_id`, `row_key`, `column`) in both JSON and human output when `!args.explicit`, keeping full values under `--explicit`.

- Running `rvl old new --key <pii_col> --json` without `--explicit` emits zero raw key values or raw column names in `contributors` (uses deterministic ordinal refs or `RVL_REDACTION_KEY` HMAC).
- Human default output likewise redacts contributor row keys and column names without `--explicit`.
- `--explicit` continues to emit full `row_id`, `row_key`, `column`, `old`, `new`, `delta`.
- Regression test with canary key value asserts zero canary occurrences in default numeric JSON and human output.

title: P1: JSONL decimals can shift numeric verdicts via serde_json f64 parsing
description: Read-only audit finding (2026-11-26, no source edits): production cargo tree -e features,normal resolves serde_json 1.0.149 with default + preserve_order, but without float_roundtrip, arbitrary_precision, or raw_value. rvl src/tabular_input.rs:16-70 routes .jsonl/.ndjson through cmdrvl-tabular; tabular src/jsonl_reader.rs:116-120 parses each line as Value and :143-153 converts a decimal Number through as_f64()+canon_f64. rvl then parses the rendered CSV numerically in src/orchestrator.rs:1013-1019, so a 16-19 digit decimal can become the adjacent f64 value before tolerance/verdict, and the resulting numeric details/output are also affected. rvl witness/ledger JSON Values are a secondary possible hash/replay surface. Fix should preserve decimal lexemes or enable the family-approved float-roundtrip/exact path without changing existing output/hash contracts silently. No released rvl binary was present locally, so this audit is code-read only. NOT VERIFIED: no build, test, release-binary reproduction, or fix was run.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
JSON-number precision family design (design-only; no product files, Cargo manifests, dependencies, releases, or tests changed).

Scope and evidence read:
- bd-uyp rvl: released 0.9.2 JSONL reproduced a 985085759598861.85 -> .9 pair as REAL_CHANGE (exit 1) while the exact-decimal delta is .05 and the CSV control is NO_REAL_CHANGE. A temporary float_roundtrip feature made that tolerance case pass, but the required collision gate then showed distinct JSONL key IDs 9007199254740992.1 and .2 collapsing to one key (the JSONL result became NO_REAL_CHANGE while CSV still refused E_KEY_MISMATCH), and distinct free-text values were also hidden. Therefore float_roundtrip is not the family fix.
- bd-al68 shape: released 0.10.1 JSONL high-precision keys 9007199254740992.1 and .2 became one overlap/duplicate verdict while the CSV control remained unique.
- bd-0ml pack: released 0.7.2 rendered adjacent high-precision report contributions 9007199254740992.1 and .2 both as 9007199254740992, while a nearby control rendered differently. The sealed bytes/hash were not changed by this render-only observation.
- bd-px5 hash: released 0.6.0 emitted byte-identical JSON for distinct 9007199254740992.1/.2 input values, and rounded 985085759598861.85/.9 differently. The raw file bytes_hash itself was unchanged.
- bd-ddq assess: released 0.4.1 treated artifact/policy pairs with 9007199254740992.1 and .2 as matching in both directions; an independent Decimal oracle says they differ.
- bd-9oi tabular: JSONL goes through serde_json::Value, then Number::as_f64() and canon_f64() before Cell::from_bytes(); this is the shared loss point for rvl and shape.
- bd-8v1 lock: raw lock JSON is Value-parsed before self-hash canonicalization. Required typed fields are u64, but unknown numeric members are included in the lock.v0 self-hash and can collide. The released 0.7.1 binary accepted distinct unknown decimals 9007199254740992.1/.2 as the same computed lock hash. I found bd-8v1 on origin/main; this checkout's stale local bead database calls the corresponding record bd-wsl. No released hash should be silently invalidated.
- bd-00dy twinning was intentionally not analyzed, per the request.

Where text is lost and what must be exact:
1. tabular: JSONL Value parsing loses the number token before json_cell(); Cell currently stores bytes, so preserve the original JSON number token there. CSV/TSV already receive source bytes; Parquet/XLSX have their own typed-to-text rules and are not fixed by JSONL parsing.
2. rvl: read_as_csv() receives the rounded Cell bytes and reparses them in the CSV comparison pipeline. Key identity must use the original token bytes (so 1.0, 1.00, and 1e0 remain distinct identifiers unless an explicit key policy says otherwise). Numeric comparison/tolerance must use exact decimal values, not f64; reports, refusal evidence, capsule input bytes, and new witness material must not invent rounded values. Existing ordinary output should remain byte-stable; affected verdicts and their dependent values necessarily change.
3. shape: the same tabular-to-Cell boundary feeds key uniqueness/overlap and numeric scans. Key identity needs source-token exactness; numeric classification/comparison needs exact decimal semantics. Corrected JSON/human reasons, capsules, canonical input bytes, and hashes for newly processed affected inputs can change; raw source-file hashes and existing capsule bytes do not.
4. assess: artifact policy_signals are serde_json::Value and policy signal conditions are compared with Value equality. The artifact JSON and policy YAML numeric token is therefore rounded before the exact-match decision. The verdict must become exact under the chosen policy semantics. Existing artifact bytes and their hashes are not rewritten; new decisions/serialized evidence for affected values can change.
5. hash: reader.rs parses the input object to Value and reserializes the enriched object. Raw file hashing is already byte hashing and must not change. Pass-through JSON values must keep their source number token; affected default JSONL output bytes change, while ordinary output and bytes_hash stay stable.
6. pack: render.rs parses report members to Value and converts contribution/share through as_f64(). Exact report values must be retained through render. Existing archive/member bytes, member hashes, and pack IDs stay unchanged; render output for affected reports changes, including HTML/Markdown numeric text.
7. lock: verify/self_hash parses raw JSON to Value and cmdrvl-core::sorted_compact serializes the parsed number. Typed lock fields remain exact today. Unknown numeric members are the self-hash risk. Existing lock.v0 documents must continue to verify, including historical hashes made with the old rounded path; changing the canonical bytes for those documents without a compatibility rule is not acceptable.

Options:
- float_roundtrip: improves f64 parser round-trip accuracy, but still creates f64 Numbers. The rvl collision test proves it does not preserve identifier identity and can suppress real text changes. Reject as the family solution.
- serde_json arbitrary_precision: preserves non-integer number text in Number instead of f64, but it changes serde_json::Value semantics package-wide. Number derives equality over its internal representation: integer 1 remains an integer, while 1.0, 1.00, and 1e0 are retained as distinct strings; those three are not equal to each other, and 1 is not equal to 1.0. It gives lexical preservation, not the required context-specific mathematical comparison. Cargo features are additive/unified for one serde_json package in a consumer graph: enabling arbitrary_precision through cmdrvl-core would also affect direct serde_json uses in rvl, shape, pack, lock, and tabular where versions unify. Do not enable it globally.
- RawValue / source text: a private RawValue or equivalent token-preserving parser is the right narrow ingestion/pass-through mechanism. It distinguishes source lexemes and avoids Value round-tripping, but it does not provide numeric ordering, tolerance, arithmetic, or a policy for numeric identifiers by itself.
- Shared exact-decimal type in cmdrvl-core: add a zero-I/O, wasm-safe exact decimal representation/parser (prefer no new third-party dependency), carrying both the validated source lexeme and a normalized comparison form. Expose separate operations: source identity/hash bytes; mathematical compare/equality; checked arithmetic/finite conversion only at explicitly lossy boundaries; deterministic canonical decimal serialization. Keep serde_json Value for unrelated control/schema data. This is the recommended approach.

Recommended semantics and operator decisions:
A. Numeric key/identifier identity: RECOMMEND source-token identity. 1.0, 1.00, and 1e0 are distinct key bytes; string-like IDs must never be compared as f64. Decide whether any named key column may opt into mathematical numeric identity; recommendation is no by default.
B. Numeric measurements/policy comparison: RECOMMEND mathematical exact-decimal equality/order, so 1.0 == 1.00 == 1e0 for measurement and assess policy values, while preserving the original token for display/pass-through. Decide whether tolerances and derived statistics must be exact-decimal end-to-end; recommendation is yes for verdicts, with f64 only as a documented final presentation fallback.
C. Pass-through/canonical output: RECOMMEND preserve the original token when a tool is copying an input number. For newly derived values, use one documented normalized decimal form. Existing unaffected values must keep their bytes; affected values are deliberate output changes. Decide whether rvl/shape reports should show preserved source spelling or normalized derived decimals; recommendation: source spelling for pass-through fields, normalized exact decimals for derived fields.
D. lock.v0 compatibility: RECOMMEND a two-path transition. New exact-token canonicalization must be used for newly created locks, while verification must accept the historical sorted_compact/rounded hash for an existing lock whose stored hash matches it; exact verification must be tried first. This keeps all existing lock.v0 files verifiable, but intentionally preserves a legacy compatibility path. Decide whether to introduce an explicit lock_hash_scheme/lock.v1 marker; recommendation is to do so before removing legacy acceptance. Do not rewrite published lock_hash values in place.
E. feature policy: RECOMMEND no global arbitrary_precision switch and no reliance on float_roundtrip for identity. Raw token preservation should be private to the reader/pass-through paths; the shared exact-decimal API should own semantic comparisons.

Adoption order:
1. cmdrvl-core: specify and test the exact-decimal API, source-vs-mathematical semantics, and lock compatibility helpers; no consumer pin bump yet.
2. cmdrvl-tabular (bd-9oi): preserve JSONL number lexemes in Cell/open_bytes without changing CSV/TSV/Parquet/XLSX behavior.
3. rvl (bd-uyp) and shape (bd-al68): use raw identity for keys and exact decimals for numeric comparison; update only affected golden outputs and witness/capsule semantics.
4. assess (bd-ddq): use exact decimals for policy signal numeric equality while preserving non-numeric Value behavior and input spelling.
5. hash (bd-px5): preserve source numeric tokens in enriched JSON; leave raw bytes_hash and non-JSON behavior unchanged.
6. pack (bd-0ml): retain exact report numbers through render; archive verification/sealing bytes remain raw.
7. lock (bd-8v1): implement the version/dual-verification decision last, with explicit tests against released lock.v0 and no invalidation of existing self-hashes.

Hash/output impact summary:
- Must change for affected new inputs: rvl/shape verdicts and derived report/capsule bytes, hash pass-through JSON, assess decisions/evidence, pack rendered numeric text, and any newly created witness IDs whose canonical input contains the corrected number.
- Must not change: raw input bytes_hash values, existing immutable capsules/archives/pack member hashes, existing witness lines/IDs, ordinary unaffected output, and existing lock.v0 verification.
- Potentially changes only for newly created lock documents containing unknown decimal members: lock_hash bytes. Published lock.v0 hashes must remain verifiable through the compatibility path; no in-place rewrite.

Not verified here: no product implementation, dependency change, build/test/clippy run, full format matrix, or new release. This comment is the design decision record requested for bd-uyp; the other bead pointers are the scope map above.

title: P0: rvl mixes incompatible units across numeric columns in unscaled L1 ranking
description: rvl currently sums abs(delta) across all common numeric columns into a single unscaled total_change. comments.text:
bd-zid Phase 1 reproduce/design evidence (no product code, docs, dependency, or cargo changes).

Released binary and provenance:
- Downloaded v0.9.2 for x86_64-apple-darwin with:
  gh release download v0.9.2 --repo cmdrvl/rvl --pattern 'rvl-v0.9.2-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz' --pattern SHA256SUMS --dir release
  (cd release && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing)
  Result: checksum OK; archive SHA-256 0bd63124e4191d821adbf2acb424875d077118779de28bbebb56ab0ed7e1f2c; binary reports rvl 0.9.2.
- Synthetic cases were mixed-old.csv/mixed-new.csv (id A, balance 1000000 -> 1000100, rate 5.0 -> 0.0), rate-only-old.csv/rate-only-new.csv, and single-column include_columns profiles. The balance delta is 100 and the rate delta is -5; rvl cannot know whether 5.0 means percent, rate points, or 500 bps.

Reproduction of the bead example:
- Command: release/rvl cases/mixed-old.csv cases/mixed-new.csv --key id --no-witness
  Result: exit 1, REAL CHANGE. Human output says 1 cell explains 95.2% of total numeric change; the sole default contributor is redacted. It reports ranking abs(delta) (unscaled), threshold 95.0%, tolerance 1e-9, 1 aligned row, 2 numeric columns, 2 checked cells.
- Command: release/rvl cases/mixed-old.csv cases/mixed-new.csv --key id --json --no-witness
  Result: exit 1, JSON outcome REAL_CHANGE; counts numeric_cells_changed=2; metrics total_change=105.0, max_abs_delta=100.0, top_k_coverage=1.0; the emitted prefix contributor has share 0.9523809523809523 (100/105). top_k_coverage is 1.0 because both cells are within the top-25 cap, while the displayed contributor prefix stops after the 95% threshold.
- With --explicit, the displayed contributor is A.balance, old 1000000.0, new 1000100.0, delta/contribution 100.0; the rate cell is in the tail. Thus “completely hides” is true for the default 95% contributor prefix, but not for counts, total_change, or max_abs_delta.
- Commands with --threshold 0.96 and --threshold 0.99 both remained exit 1 REAL_CHANGE and emitted both contributors; --exhaustive --explicit --json emitted both cells. No wrong exit verdict was observed in this two-cell example; the ranking/prefix is the failure. A larger corpus could still hit the documented E_DIFFUSE coverage refusal when the top-25 prefix cannot reach the requested threshold, but I did not claim that as reproduced here.
- The bead’s “-500 bps” wording is domain interpretation, not an rvl observation. The program sees only numeric 5.0 -> 0.0 and has no unit metadata.

Tolerance:
- Command: release/rvl cases/mixed-old.csv cases/mixed-new.csv --key id --tolerance 5 --json --no-witness
  Result: exit 1 REAL_CHANGE; rate delta exactly 5 is suppressed by the documented <= tolerance rule, so total_change=100.0 and numeric_cells_changed=1.
- Command: release/rvl cases/rate-only-old.csv cases/rate-only-new.csv --key id --tolerance 10 --json --no-witness
  Result: exit 0 NO_REAL_CHANGE; total_change=0.0, numeric_cells_changed=0, max_abs_delta=5.0. This is the existing absolute-tolerance contract: it can suppress a small-unit move, but it is not specifically caused by mixed-unit aggregation.

Profile scoping:
- --profile cases/balance-only.yaml --json --no-witness: exit 1 REAL_CHANGE; one common numeric column, total_change=100.0, contributor share=1.0.
- --profile cases/rate-only.yaml --json --no-witness: exit 1 REAL_CHANGE; one common numeric column, total_change=5.0, contributor share=1.0.
This is a practical workaround when the operator deliberately scopes one unit family, but the released profile format only has include_columns/key/column_types; it does not declare units or make a cross-unit comparison safe.

Source verification:
- docs/PLAN_RVL.md defines contribution as abs(new-old) after tolerance, total_change as the L1 sum across numeric cells, and v0 as intentionally unscaled (around lines 112-117 and 319-327).
- src/diff/tolerance.rs computes raw delta and absolute contribution; src/diff/heap.rs adds each contribution directly to total_change; src/diff/coverage.rs evaluates the top-contributor prefix against that total.
- src/profile.rs scopes included columns but has no unit/scale field.
- src/output/json.rs emits total_change, max_abs_delta, top_k_coverage, and contributor shares without unit metadata.
The bead’s core description is correct. The narrower correction is that the current implementation does not lose the rate from all output or from the total; it loses it from the default thresholded contributor prefix and can make its importance appear negligible.

Baseline artifact effects:
- Command: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1700000000 EPISTEMIC_WITNESS=cases/witness-baseline-2.jsonl release/rvl cases/mixed-old.csv cases/mixed-new.csv --key id --json --capsule-dir cases/capsule-baseline-2 --explicit
  Result: exit 1; capsule manifest rvl.capsule.v0 records total_change=105.0, one emitted top contributor, coverage 0.9523809523809523, and output hash blake3:c3ce043ff935f15e4b09fb67d825030972a3a60aef76336c3af2d52a4b23c141. The witness records params plus output_hash and witness id. Any implementation that changes ranking, metrics, verdict, or output bytes changes the capsule output hash/capsule_id and witness output_hash/id; adding a mode/profile also changes replay args or params. With SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixed, this remains deterministic.

Design options and evidence:

1. Per-column ranking/summary. Keep raw abs(delta) per cell but rank each column separately or emit a per-column subtotal/rank alongside the current global ranking. This can surface the rate without claiming unit comparability. A summary-only version need not change REAL_CHANGE/NO_REAL_CHANGE or exit codes, but changes human/JSON bytes and likely requires new optional schema fields; repurposing existing total_change would break its documented meaning. Capsules and witnesses change whenever output changes, including output hashes and ids. It has no unit false-positive claim, but it cannot decide whether a cross-column total or threshold is semantically valid, so it can still produce misleading global verdicts if that remains the decision metric. Deterministic with a specified column/name tie-break.

2. Numeric normalization. Possible policies include relative change abs(delta)/max(abs(old), abs(new), floor), baseline-relative change, or a robust per-column scale such as a declared unit scale. Zero baselines require a defined infinity/special case; negatives need abs-based denominators and sign-change rules; tiny values need a floor; huge values risk overflow or loss of resolution unless bounded. Any floor/clamp changes ranking and must be part of the contract. Normalized values can make REAL_CHANGE/NO_REAL_CHANGE and E_DIFFUSE outcomes, exit 0/1/2, threshold coverage, contributors, and total_change differ. Reusing v0 fields would silently change schema semantics; a versioned or explicitly marked normalized report is safer. Capsules/witnesses, lock/profile-derived JSON, and output hashes change. Deterministic if the exact formula, tie-breaks, and finite-value handling are specified, but it still does not identify units.

3. Mixed-scale heuristic warning. Detect magnitude ratios, column ranges, or contribution concentration and emit a deterministic warning while preserving the current verdict. This avoids an immediate exit-code break, but has false positives for same-unit columns with different legitimate ranges and false negatives for different units with similar magnitudes. The warning changes human/JSON output and therefore capsule/witness bytes; adding a warning field requires schema/e2e updates, while stderr-only warnings can still break snapshots and scripts. It must be described as a heuristic, never as unit detection. Determinism is achievable by sorting columns and using fixed thresholds.

4. Refuse unless explicitly scoped. If a deterministic heuristic says a comparison is suspicious, refuse with a new typed refusal unless the user supplies a unit-scoped profile or an explicit legacy --unscaled flag. This makes a possible mixed-unit error visible and gives exit 2, but heuristic false positives can reject valid comparisons and false negatives remain. A refusal code/JSON shape, human message, and CLI flag change output/schema and capsule/witness records; existing cmdrvl e2e cases that currently expect exit 0/1 or rvl.v0 output would need updates. The explicit --unscaled path preserves old behavior and determinism, but does not make it safe.

5. Explicit profile-declared unit groups/scales. Extend profiles with operator-provided unit groups and/or scale factors and require normalized cross-column aggregation only when those declarations exist. This avoids pretending that rvl can infer units; wrong user metadata remains possible, but it is auditable and deterministic. It changes profile schema/hash, output semantics, and likely needs an output/report version or an explicit mode; capsules include changed profile args/hash and witnesses include changed params/output hashes. Existing profiles without the fields can retain current scoped behavior; a mixed unscoped default can refuse or remain legacy only behind --unscaled. This is the only option here that provides a principled normalization input, but it requires profile-tool and consumer coordination.

Recommendation:
Adopt explicit profile-declared unit groups/scales for any normalized cross-column ranking, and do not infer units from magnitude. Make legacy raw aggregation an explicit --unscaled mode, and have an unscoped mixed-unit candidate refuse with a typed exit-2 result rather than silently choosing a heuristic. Keep the existing raw total and verdict as a clearly marked compatibility mode during a versioned transition. Add per-column subtotals/ranking so a report remains useful even when normalization is unavailable. This minimizes false claims, keeps deterministic behavior, and makes the deliberate output/schema/capsule/witness changes reviewable.

Compatibility and consumer impact:
The cmdrvl e2e suite and any consumers that parse rvl.v0, compare human/JSON golden bytes, or verify capsule/witness hashes can break if current fields change, if warning/refusal fields are added, or if exit 0/1 becomes exit 2. The read-only search found no unit declaration in the released profile contract; no e2e or consumer suite was run in this reproduce-only phase.

- No real filing/table with declared units was tested, and no released non-macOS asset was run.
